title: Read by position with iloc
summary: iloc selects by zero-based positions. Its row and column numbers describe where values are placed.
introduction: iloc selects by zero-based positions. Its row and column numbers describe where values are placed. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain read by position with iloc
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: iloc selects by zero-based positions. Its row and column numbers describe where values are placed.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

print(df.iloc[0, 1])
blocks.title: Read by position with iloc

blocks.text: The output is 8: the first row and second column.

blocks.text: Do not pass a column name to iloc when it expects a position.
